environmentComparison.claim: Recorded browser revision, GPU/software flags, runner CPU/kernel/image/memory and native surface match. This records machine class; it does not observe transient co-tenant load or prove runner stability.

findings: Candidate fails exactly one reported budget: desktop map-pan callback p95=36.3ms against strict<35ms.
Desktop baseline/candidate each have191 RAF callbacks and192 intervals including boundaries; intervals>=35ms rise9 to10. This crosses the95th-percentile order statistic.
Desktop max callback gap40.3→42.0ms; neither has gaps>50ms, longtasks, unexpected CLS or invalid observation.
Desktop native drag648.38→669.96ms; slow intervals cluster during native mouse moves and at release. This is temporal correlation, not a function-level profile.
Both traces arrays are empty and instrumented=false. There is no current trace, compositor presentation sample, scene draw timing, worker warmup start/end or network timing witness in these receipts.

A map-warmup overlap cannot be confirmed or ruled out from these receipts. The candidate production worker bounds warmup to12s and cancels it for update, but this fact alone does not locate warmup during the failed pan.
The evidence supports a borderline performance failure and no identified specific new hotspot. It does not justify changing a threshold, hiding the failure or claiming an already fixed regression.
limitations: requestAnimationFrame callbackHz is not compositor/presented FPS. Native input-to-next-frame is not field INP.
The historical baseline source differs from the candidate; one passed and one failed sample do not establish causal regression or statistical runner noise.
No CI rerun, production change, test weakening or additional browser runtime was performed for this analysis.
